messages:
jamie: FYI customer ACME reported a sudden p99 jump on hosted inference for model-redwood-v1 around 11:22 UTC. Baseline was ~120ms, p99 spiked to ~720ms. Seen across a few nodes in pool-3.

sasha: Can you paste a sample request + headers? Also which runtime config for continuous-batcher is active?

jamie: sample single-request body (sanitized):

```json
{
  "input": "short prompt: summarize",
  "max_tokens": 64,
  "temperature": 0.0
}
```

Headers: auth ok, tenant=acme-prod, route=model/redwood-v1.
Config snapshot from /configs/batcher/pool-3:
```yaml
mode: continuous
max_batch_size: 32
min_batch_size: 1
hold_timeout_ms: 30
grace_window_ms: 60
adaptive_grace: false
```

taylor: Thanks. From logs it looks like tiny, bursty traffic from ACME (lots of single-token/short prompts) is causing many 1-2 item batches. The batcher is extending hold time because of grace_window_ms and the grace isn't being satisfied so we get long tails. Seeing coalescing latency for requests that landed just before batch flush.

priyanka: This is classic hold-vs-size tradeoff. Two quick mitigations: 1) reduce hold_timeout_ms to 5-10ms for pool-3 to avoid long waits for stragglers, 2) enable adaptive_grace so the batcher can shrink grace when arrival rate is low. Also consider bumping min_batch_size to 2 for this pool so pure singletons don't keep waiting for grace window.

jamie: I'm going to try a canary change against pool-3 nodes (two nodes) with:

```yaml
max_batch_size: 32
min_batch_size: 2
hold_timeout_ms: 8
grace_window_ms: 40
adaptive_grace: true
```

repro steps I ran locally:
1) replay ACME traffic (short prompts) via loadgen: ./loadgen --tenant acme --qps 120 --burst 20 --prompt-file acme_short.txt
2) tail logs: kubectl logs -f batcher-pool-3 --since=5m | grep batch
3) measure percentiles via /metrics endpoint (batch_latency_p50/p95/p99)

Result before change: p99 ~ 720ms. After applying canary config on two nodes and re-running the replay for 10m: p99 dropped to ~190ms, p95 ~80ms. CPU/gpu utilization steady.

infra-bot: config-canary: rolled batcher config to pool-3 nodes (node-7,node-8) id=cfg-2026-03-17-007.

oncall: Good. Keep an eye on errors — reducing hold_timeout could increase small-batch inefficiencies and raise token cost per request. Watch error-rate, qps, and cost-per-1000 tokens. If error-rate > 0.5% in next 30m, revert.

priyanka: Also add a short-lived alert on batch_coalesce_ratio and avg_batch_size so we can see whether min_batch_size=2 causes too many immediate small batches. If it does, we can instead use adaptive_min= true to only enforce min when arrival rate supports it.

jamie: Noted. I'll push canary to remaining pool-3 nodes in 10m if metrics look good. Will include a note to customer support telling ACME we've applied a mitigation and asking for confirmation on their side.

sasha: One more thing — we saw a handful of auth-401 errors correlated with the spike window earlier; that looks unrelated but file a support ticket in case they retry aggressively.

jamie: Filed support ticket SUP-9142 referencing the config canary and attached replay logs.

oncall: LGTM. Follow-up: schedule a 1h post-mortem if p99 doesn't stabilize to baseline after full rollout. Otherwise we can document this as a config recipe for short-prompt workloads. :thumbsup:

jamie: thanks all — will update here after 30m. :coffee:
